projects.title: CodeBase
projects.summary: Know how a project works, not just where its files are.
projects.description: Open a folder or a GitHub link and CodeBase finds the project's architecture, traces each user journey end to end, explains every version in plain words, and hands any AI chat exactly the slice of code it needs.
projects.problem: Free AI chats can read only a few thousand words at a time. Paste too little and the AI guesses; paste too much and it forgets the start. Either way, a fix in one file breaks another.
projects.idea: Be the librarian, not the expert. CodeBase knows the whole project and builds one block of text that fits the chat: instructions, a project brief, the task, the few files that matter, and outlines of the files around them.
projects.approach: Architecture, flows and history come from reading the code and Git, without running it and without AI. It ships as one small executable for Windows, macOS and Linux that serves a local web interface.
projects.details: Offline and free: no account, no API key, no telemetry. Nothing leaves the computer until the user pastes it somewhere.

projects.title: Understudy
projects.summary: Record Android tests by clicking, feed them Excel data, run them with Maestro.
projects.description: A local app for Android UI test automation on top of the Maestro CLI. Version 2 of what began as X-Maestro Flow Runner: click an element on the phone screen, choose an action, and decide whether a typed value is fixed text or an Excel column.
projects.problem: Maestro has no Excel data-driven testing, little feedback about which step is running, and no run history. Twenty data sets meant twenty copies of a flow or twenty command lines.
projects.approach: Record in one window, run any flows with any Excel rows, watch every step live, and read one report per test with run comparison and flaky-test detection. Screenshots are compressed on the phone, about ten times smaller than PNG.
projects.details: Everything runs on the PC: no account, no cloud, no upload. Light and dark themes.

projects.title: ResearchTrail
projects.summary: Keep what you read next to what you build.
projects.description: A local research notebook for students and independent researchers. Paste a paper link and it becomes a structured card; point it at a project folder and every save of the code is kept. Stage by stage, it shows what each paper did next to what your code does.
projects.problem: Three months into a thesis the questions are always the same: which paper did this preprocessing step come from, and why did accuracy drop between two drafts? Reference managers don't know your code, and Git doesn't know your papers.
projects.approach: Paper cards record data, preprocessing, features, model, training and evaluation, each item linked to its source sentence. Code history works without Git, and a per-stage comparison matrix puts every paper beside your own work.
projects.limitations: Working draft (v0.1). The core loop works end to end and has tests, but it is not yet something to rely on for a thesis.

projects.title: QA automation frameworks
projects.summary: Two behaviour-driven UI test frameworks in C#, Playwright and Reqnroll.
projects.description: End-to-end BDD frameworks for OrangeHRM (an HR system, 12 scenarios) and ParaBank (an online bank), with smoke, regression and E2E suites, multi-role flows and HTML reports.
projects.approach: Gherkin scenarios bound to C# steps, page objects with selectors kept in one place, Excel-driven test data, tag-based login hooks, and cross-browser runs headed locally or headless in GitHub Actions.
projects.details: Built to stay stable on a slow shared demo site: explicit visibility waits, navigation retries, and autocomplete handling that checks the selection actually took.

projects.title: Koineze
projects.summary: A pocket ledger for everyday taka, logged in two taps.
projects.description: Tracks daily spending, salary, bank, bKash and cash balances, loans, big purchases and saving plans. It began as a PHP and MySQL web app and was rebuilt as an installable mobile web app.
projects.idea: Answer the questions that matter on the way home: how much is left, and was today an expensive day? It knows the office week, so it can show what an office day really costs compared with a home day.
projects.details: Private by design: each database row is locked to its owner, with no ads, trackers or third-party scripts. Old Notepad notes can be pasted in and become real entries.

projects.title: NYC taxi trip analysis
projects.summary: Geospatial and temporal patterns in large-scale New York taxi data.
projects.description: Predicting taxi trip duration with PySpark, comparing classical machine learning with deep learning, and clustering trips to find patterns across the city.
projects.approach: Cleaned invalid records, engineered features such as trip duration, distance, hour of day and day of week, then trained linear regression, gradient-boosted trees, CNN and LSTM models and ran K-means clustering.
projects.results: Gradient-boosted trees reached 70.4% accuracy within a 10% range, and LSTM 71.4%. Demand peaked on Fridays and Saturdays, and weekday trips ran longer because of traffic.

projects.title: Object detection from satellite images
projects.summary: Finding and locating objects in high-resolution satellite imagery.
projects.description: Trained YOLOv5 and Fast R-CNN detectors on satellite imagery with COCO-format annotations, from preprocessing to inference with bounding-box overlays.

projects.title: Renewable energy and weather
projects.summary: How weather shapes renewable energy output, modelled with LSTM and HMM.
projects.description: Predicting hourly energy generation from temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation and solar irradiance, and uncovering hidden weather regimes.
projects.results: The LSTM reached R² 0.87 with an MAE of 170.2; the HMM also reached R² 0.87 and helped reveal latent weather states.

projects.title: Bengali sentiment analysis
projects.summary: Deep learning for sentiment in a low-resource language.
projects.description: Classifying Bengali comments by sentiment and comparing CNN, RNN and LSTM models with a logistic regression baseline, using TF-IDF and bag-of-words features.
projects.results: Logistic regression came out ahead (41.7% accuracy); the deep models underperformed with the data available.
projects.limitations: Limited labelled data and unstable training held the neural models back. Better data and model design are the next step.

research.title: Adaptive Diffusion-Based Cloud Removal in Satellite Imagery
research.venue: 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
research.objective: Remove clouds from satellite imagery with diffusion-based deep learning models, reconstructing what lies underneath.
contributions: Developed a cloud-removal pipeline using Stable Diffusion inpainting.
Preprocessed satellite images with cloud masking and normalisation.
Evaluated reconstructions with pixel-wise loss against ground-truth images.

research.title: Evidence-Aware Financial Fraud Detection: Delayed Labels, Entity History, and Model Choice
research.venue: The Journal of Finance and Data Science
research.objective: Study how delayed fraud labels, the history of each entity, and the choice of model shape what a fraud detector can honestly claim.
